title: export.start
description: Writes a WAV file of a clip (kind clip, target.placementId), a track (kind track, target.trackId) or the master mix (kind master, no target) as a job of kind export, under the export contract of PROTOCOL.md section 19: the path is checked before the job starts; an export that would hold no audio (a track without clips, a master mix in which no clip is heard) fails at once with INVALID_ARGUMENT(nothing_to_export), and so does a job whose clips were all removed while it waited; loaded source files and project media are never written (INVALID_ARGUMENT(target_is_loaded_media)), and when the identity of one of them cannot be determined, for example because its volume is not available, the export is refused with IO_ERROR(read_failed) (section 20.3 rule 4); ifExists decides what happens to an existing target: with error, a target that already exists makes the call fail at once with ALREADY_EXISTS(target_exists), starting no job, and a target that appears before the final rename makes the job fail with the same error; the UI and this API share one export lock (BUSY(export_in_progress)); the job waits for analysis and rendering to settle (NOT_READY(export_wait_timeout), ANALYSIS_FAILED(f0_failed), RENDER_FAILED(render_chunk_failed)); render blocks that OpenTune has set aside for a delayed retry are drained first, and when they cannot be drained the job fails with the same retryable NOT_READY(export_wait_timeout) (section 19 rules 6 and 7); and for a content whose time grid is not the identity also for its time-stretched audio, which ends the job early with NOT_READY(export_dry_stretched) when the content would be exported uncorrected and with NOT_READY(export_stretch_dropped) when the stretched audio is not built (section 19 rule 6); the revision of every content is recorded once all contents are ready and the file starts to be written, so a revision that changes while the job waits (for example because an analysis finishes) is no conflict, while a revision that changes after it was recorded, before the final check, fails the job with REVISION_CONFLICT(changed_during_export) and leaves the target untouched; contents exported uncorrected are listed in dryContents. contents lists the revision of every content in the file, as the job recorded it when all contents were ready, so that a client can tell whether edits made after export.start are in the file. A call with the same normalized params as an export job that is not terminal returns that job. The call itself changes no project state: its result hands the work to the job, whose result is jobResult. dryContents[].reason is unvoiced (no voiced audio), nothingToRender, or analysisFailed (with allowDry). processing members that cannot be determined are null and named in processing.nullReasons.

path.description: Absolute path of the WAV file to write; the extension must be .wav.

allowDry.description: Export a content whose analysis failed uncorrected instead of failing (PROTOCOL.md section 19 rule 6).

path.description: The file that was written; with ifExists rename it may differ from the requested path.

startTimelineSec.description: 0 for master and track exports, the clip's start for a clip export.

contents.description: The revision of every content the file holds, recorded when all contents were ready (PROTOCOL.md section 19 rule 8).

hybridMode.description: Whether OpenTune's hybrid mode is on. With it on, OpenTune renders small corrections with a pitch shift of the audio instead of the vocoder, so the corrected pitch that results report can differ from what is heard (informative, PROTOCOL.md section 19, "Hybrid mode").
